svg.title: Why the argument stops at 9/4
svg.desc: For a hypothetical character that rates n-by-n matrix multiplication at n to the power omega, the profile P(a,a) must lie between the proven floor a^(4/3) and the rank ceiling (2a-1)^(3/omega). The chart plots ceiling divided by floor against a on log-log axes. For omega = 3, 2.7, 2.5 and 2.371 the ratio eventually drops below 1, which is impossible; the crossings are near a = 6, 29, 510 and 400,000. For omega = 9/4 the ratio rises towards 2^(4/3), about 2.52, and never drops below 1.
svg.text: Suppose some character rated n×n matrix multiplication at n^ω. The proof traps the profile P(a,a) between a floor and a ceiling:
floor a^(4/3) from the two tensor constructions, ceiling (2a−1)^(3/ω) from the cheap rank of polynomial multiplication.
Plotted: ceiling ÷ floor. If it ever drops below 1, that ω is impossible.
a = number of coefficients in each polynomial (log scale)
Impossible: the floor would be above the ceiling
ω = 9/4 never crosses: the ratio climbs towards 2^(4/3) ≈ 2.52
Dots on the line “1” mark where each hypothetical ω first becomes impossible. Every curve starts at 1 when a = 1. Floor: the paper’s Lemma 5.1. Ceiling: its eq. (4.5).
